newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault says merger with Aerospatiale on track.
newsitem.headline: Dassault says merger with Aerospatiale on track.

text.p: French combat-plane maker Dassault Aviation said on Friday merger talks with state-owned Aerospatiale were on track and a joint proposal had been given to the government on the outlines of their linkup.
"They deposited a draft (plan) for the government's approval that was sponsored jointly" by Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot and Dassault Aviation boss Serge Dassault, a Dassault spokesman said.
Aerospatiale said it could not comment on progress toward the merger aimed at creating a single large air and defence company.
The spokesman for family-owned Dassault said he expected a government announcement in early January but would not specify its nature.
"The conversations (between Michot and Dassault) have gone well and the government should be able "to announce something interesting" in early January.
A report in the newspaper Le Monde said Defence Minister Charles Millon would announce the new industrial set-up of the merged group at the start of January.
The newspaper said talks were still continuing with the state on the financial terms of the merger.

Earlier this week, Industry Minister Franck Borotra called for a speeding up of the merger to meet the challenge posed by the linkup between Boeing-McDonnell Douglas creating the world's biggest aerospace company.
The centre-right government had given the two companies until the end of the year to seal the details of their merger.
But Aerospatiale said last summer it thought legal formalities would drag out the process and that the new company would not start-up until mid-1997 at the earliest.

The government sought the merger between the two pillars of France's aerospace industry to improve the country's ability to compete with other national aerospace industries and increase opportunities with the rest of Europe on defence ventures.
